test_title: SSC MTS 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 10 Feb, 2026 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
Which of the following idiom given in the alternatives has the meaning?
An offer made without conditions or restrictions, and requires nothing in return.
solution: The correct answer is: **Option 3 i.e. With no strings attached**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ • The idiom **"With no strings attached"** means an offer made without conditions, restrictions, or requiring anything in return. (बिना किसी शर्त के) • **Example:** The company offered a free trial of its software with no strings attached. • This idiom is often used in situations where something is given freely and the giver does not expect anything in return. (यह तब उपयोग किया जाता है जब कुछ बिना अपेक्षा के दिया जाता है।) Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 3 i.e. With no strings attached**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences: • **Keep one on a string** (किसी को अपने वश में रखना): To control or manipulate someone as if pulling their strings. • **Example:** He kept her on a string, never committing to the relationship but not letting her go either. • **Loosen the apron strings** (स्वतंत्र होने देना): To allow someone (often a child) to become independent. • **Example:** It's time for her parents to loosen the apron strings and let her make her own decisions. • **Loosen the purse strings** (खर्च करने के लिए तैयार होना): To be willing to spend money or increase expenditure. • **Example:** The government decided to loosen the purse strings to fund new infrastructure projects. 1ba:Tb0a, The correct answer is: **Option 1 i.e. "Said when someone suddenly comes to realize or understand something"**.
